purpose: Candidate-only Ollaya scoring tuned from v002's thresholded training-set errors.
model: Read from the repository .env key OLLAYA_MODEL

is_identifier.instructions: Judge only the candidate string; this tuning input contains no occurrence context. Do not invent a sentence or claim that document-specific use has been verified. Decide whether the string is an identifier-like reference to a particular person, organization, project, location, system, codeword, or named institutional/operational entity. Distinctive names and organization or operation acronyms can qualify even when abbreviated or pluralized. For this dataset's labeling convention, a formal military rank or office can count as a person/office reference when it is used as a label (for example Colonel, Commander, Lieutenant, Major, or LTC); do not reject it solely because it is not a personal name. Likewise, a recognizable action-report or military/government organization acronym can be Yes without an expansion when its form itself supports that reading. Do not treat capitalization, a generic role, an arbitrary digit suffix, or mere familiarity with a product, company, or place as proof that this document uses it as a specific entity. A familiar ordinary word remains No unless the string supports a distinct named-entity reading. When the candidate alone leaves genuine ambiguity, reflect that uncertainty in the Yes probability.

criteria.Yes: The string gives meaningful lexical evidence of a particular person or office reference, organization, project, location, system, codeword, or other named institutional/operational entity; dataset-positive formal ranks/offices and recognizable entity acronyms are included.
criteria.No: The string is ordinary prose, a generic role with no person/office-reference reading, a malformed or reference-number artifact, or only a globally recognizable product/place/person name whose use as a specific entity here cannot be established from the candidate alone.

is_operationally_significant.instructions: Using only the candidate word, decide whether its own meaning denotes a consequential military, government, security, cyber, or other operational activity, force, command, campaign, raid, capability, vulnerability, plan, designated resource, unit, or operation. A domain-specific unit, force, organization, or mission acronym may be Yes even when its expansion is unavailable; do not require an acronym to be familiar before recognizing that it is an operational label. Include direct action/force terms such as campaign, commands, forces, and raid when used as operational concepts. Do not say Yes merely because a generic word is often found in military, security, or IT writing: broad domain words, generic adjectives, and generic verbs such as military, security, secure, attack, adversarial, risk, or scan are No by themselves unless the candidate string identifies a distinct operational concept, capability, or resource. If an operational interpretation depends on missing context, do not invent it; express the uncertainty in the Yes probability.

criteria.Yes: The candidate itself identifies a specific operational activity, campaign, force/command/unit, designated organization or resource, military/security/cyber capability or vulnerability, or a domain-specific operation/unit acronym.
criteria.No: The candidate is generic everyday, management, IT, or security vocabulary, a broad domain descriptor, adjective, or action word whose operational significance depends on unavailable context, and does not itself identify a consequential operational concept.

is_common_word.instructions: Independently decide whether the candidate is an established English lexical item; do not interpret common as meaning only one of the very highest-frequency/simple words. Answer Yes for standard dictionary words and recognizable inflected, derived, or technical English words, even when they are less frequent, long, capitalized, or used as a name in another signal. Evaluate the English word/component rather than penalizing capitalization or technical subject matter. Digits, indexes, or code-like material before or after a recognizable English word do not make that word uncommon (for example 001Version or CAPACITY26); assess the recognizable English component. Widely established everyday-professional terms may also be Yes even when they look like product or platform names. Answer No only when the candidate has no clear established English word/component and is primarily an invented token, non-lexical acronym, malformed form, or code/name. Do not let identifier or operational scores decide this signal; when an ordinary English lexical reading is clear, favor Yes.

criteria.Yes: The candidate is a standard English word, recognized inflected/derived or technical English form, or contains a recognizable established English word/component; capitalization, a name-like appearance, rarity, or attached digits do not by themselves make it No.
criteria.No: The candidate is primarily an invented, malformed, or non-lexical acronym/code/name and has no clear established English lexical component.

change_rationale: The v002 threshold diagnostics showed 1,565 common-word false negatives versus only 6 false positives: ordinary English vocabulary, inflections/derivatives, and word-like terms were often kept just below 0.5, so v003 makes an established English lexical item the clear positive case and explicitly handles attached digits/components. Identifier errors were 9 false negatives and 75 false positives; v003 addresses the missed rank/office references and action-report or organization acronyms while retaining the requirement not to infer document use from capitalization or familiarity alone. Operational errors were 22 false negatives and 157 false positives; v003 calls out missed campaign/force/command/raid and acronym patterns while tightening the No case for generic domain-associated words and verbs. All three signals remain independent and the Yes/No threshold stays at 0.5. The source is word-only, so context-dependent target disagreements remain inherently limited by the input.

evaluation_provenance.target_semantics: Targets may be fractional values in [0,1]. For the requested hard diagnostic, actual is target >= 0.5, predicted is score >= 0.5, and the predict_is_* correctness flag is true exactly when actual equals predicted. Blank scores are missing, not zero, and are excluded from correct/incorrect counts.
evaluation_provenance.evaluation_scope: In-sample tuning comparison; no holdout or generalization claim.
v002_error_patterns_used_for_v003: Identifier: false negatives included formal rank/office terms (Colonel, Commander, Lieutenant, Major, LTC), government references, and action-report or organization acronyms (AARs, CONOPS). False positives concentrated on recognizable products/platforms, companies, places/people, and arbitrary acronym/digit-style tokens without candidate-only evidence of document use.

Operational significance: false negatives included military/government acronyms and unit/force/command or mission concepts (including AETHER, CapDev, DXO, PPCoE, XBD/XWB, campaign, commands, forces, and raid). False positives were broad generic domain-associated vocabulary, including security/IT descriptors and generic verbs/adjectives such as secure, attack, adversarial, risk, and scan.

Common word: 1,565 false negatives versus 6 false positives. Misses clustered on recognizable English words and inflections/derivatives, including many scores in the 0.25-0.50 range, plus tokens with attached numeric/index material; v003 favors an established English lexical reading. The small false-positive set appears context-sensitive and is not used to suppress the much larger positive class.
comparison_caveats: Each supplied file has 3,018 rows and 160 rows with all three score fields blank; these are reported as missing and not counted as predict_is_* true or false. All 160 missing rows have target_is_common_word >= 0.5.

The v001 and v002 word sets differ only by TRUE versus true; target values are unchanged. The files do not contain request/model metadata, so the supplied comparison is thresholded result-file analysis, not a confirmed same-model prompt-only comparison.
The next evaluation uses the model tag currently configured in .env (von:1.1) and candidate-only input. Any resulting metrics remain in-sample.
evaluation_provenance.comparison_status: v003 snapshot created from supplied v001/v002 threshold errors; v003 local CLI scoring and comparison are pending.
